who: Scholar of labor, race and social movements at UC Santa Barbara; PhD Sociology, UC Riverside, 1998.

evidence.says: UCSB identifies Armbruster-Sandoval as a professor in Chicana and Chicano Studies, with a 1998 sociology PhD from UC Riverside.
The 2011–2012 graduate handbook lists Ralph Armbruster-Sandoval, PhD UC Riverside, as an associate professor.
The authority identifies the author of Starving for Justice as an associate professor in Chicana and Chicano Studies at UCSB.
The matching dissertation title appears under Leah Fernandez; the faculty advisor listed is Eileen Boris.

notes: Name, institution, period and doctoral institution agree. UCSB lists Boris for Fernandez, so the AHA supervision attribution is qualified; the candidate identity is supported.

who: Historian of early modern Europe and Christianity at University of Illinois Chicago; PhD Chicago, 1990.

evidence.says: Under PhDs awarded in 2020, UIC lists Laurie Perlini’s matching Sant’Adriano dissertation and names Ralph Keen as dissertation advisor.
UIC identifies Keen as professor of history and states that he received his PhD from Chicago in 1990.
The authority identifies Ralph Keen with a Chicago PhD in history of Christianity, 1990, and the dissertation The Moral World of Philip Melanchthon.

notes: Direct student-supervisor confirmation and matching doctorate distinguish this candidate from the other Keen authorities.

who: Historian of premodern Korea at Columbia University, appointed in 2013; PhD Harvard, 2007.

evidence.says: Columbia’s 2019 student profile lists Eunsung Cho’s advisors as Lean and Kim and describes the dissertation on vinalon and Juche.
Columbia identifies Jungwon Kim as a historian of Chosŏn Korea, joining in 2013 after a Harvard PhD in 2007, and describes a Negotiating Virtue manuscript.
This authority identifies Jungwon Kim as the author of Negotiating Virtue and the Lives of Women in Late Chosŏn Korea.
The catalogue identifies that work as Jungwon Kim’s 2007 Harvard doctoral dissertation in East Asian Languages and Civilizations.
The apparently affiliation-compatible Jung Hyup Kim authority instead identifies an industrial and systems engineering professor at University of Missouri.

notes: The dissertation title, field and Harvard degree connect the Jungwon authority to the Columbia historian. The automatic Columbia agreement for Jung Hyup Kim is misleading.

who: Historian of science and technology at University of Alberta; PhD Toronto.

evidence.says: The university calendar lists Andrew G. Ede as adjunct professor of History and Classics, appointed in 2002, with MS and PhD from Toronto.
The authority identifies Andrew Ede, University of Alberta, as the author of Technology and Society and a historian of science and technology.
The 2018 university magazine identifies Ede as a historian in the Faculty of Arts and director of the science, technology and society program.

notes: University, field and Toronto doctorate support the match; the cited sources do not directly establish Lebiedowski’s supervision.

who: Historian of photography at University of Alberta; PhD Alberta.

evidence.says: Skidmore identifies herself as a photography historian and professor emerita in History and Classics, with a PhD from Alberta; publications include This Wild Spirit and Rare Merit.
Sarah Carter’s institutional CV lists Catharine Mastin’s Beyond the Artist’s Wife doctoral project with Colleen Skidmore as co-supervisor.
The authority associates Colleen Skidmore with This Wild Spirit and Rare Merit, identifying the latter’s author as professor emerita at Alberta.

notes: The matching works, Alberta affiliation and doctorate agree; Carter’s CV directly corroborates Mastin’s co-supervision.

who: Historian of Scotland, Ireland and tourism at University of Guelph since 2000; PhD Edinburgh, 2000.

evidence.says: Guelph identifies Kevin James as professor of history, on faculty since 2000, with an Edinburgh PhD in 2000 and research on Scotland, Ireland and tourism.

The authority identifies Kevin J. James as a Guelph history professor with an Edinburgh PhD in social history; works include Handloom Weavers in Ulster’s Linen Industry and Tourism, Land, and Landscape in Ireland.
Guelph lists Katie McCullough’s matching Building the Highland Empire dissertation in 2014 with Graeme Morton as advisor.

notes: Institution, period, field and doctorate identify the candidate. Guelph names Morton for McCullough, so James’s precise supervisory role is not independently confirmed.

who: Maritime historian at Memorial University’s Grenfell Campus; PhD Queen’s University.

evidence.says: The Canadian Nautical Research Society’s July 2002 newsletter identifies William Miles of Memorial University alongside his academic supervisor, Olaf Janzen.
Memorial lists Olaf Janzen as professor emeritus in Historical Studies with MA and PhD from Queen’s.
The authority identifies Olaf Uwe Janzen as professor of history at Memorial University’s Grenfell Campus and author of work on Newfoundland and British maritime strategy.

notes: The authority’s expanded name and institution agree; the society newsletter directly connects Janzen with the listed student, although earlier than the dissertation completion year.

who: Classical archaeologist and history professor at University of South Florida; PhD Torino, 2007.

evidence.says: USF lists Kaitlyn Kingsland’s matching Archaeogaming doctoral dissertation in 2023 with Davide Tanasi as professor.
USF identifies Tanasi as a history professor and director of the Institute for Digital Exploration, with a 2007 PhD from Torino.
The authority cites USF’s history faculty page, identifying Davide Tanasi as a Mediterranean archaeologist with a 2007 Torino PhD.
USF’s institutional research profile lists the Torino PhD and earlier BA and MA degrees at Catania.

notes: Direct Kingsland supervision and the LC citation to USF establish identity. AHA’s Catania doctoral-school entry differs from USF’s Torino PhD listing; Catania is documented for earlier degrees.
